newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast crudes rise with WTI, but trade flat.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast crudes rise with WTI, but trade flat.

text.p: U.S. West Coast light crude prices rose nearly $1 Monday, tracking higher domestic grades, but regional trade fizzled because buyers reassessed the cheaper market for Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude.
Exxon sold two full cargoes of ANS, the West Coast benchmark, late last week, with the last deal increasing discounts to $1.50 under West Texas Intermediate/Cushing.
In response to lower prices, BP, the biggest producer of ANS, lowered its offer 15 cents a barrel Monday to $1.30 under WTI.
Despite the wider discounts, outright ANS prices rose 95 cents a barrel, as WTI swung higher on concerns of supply disruptions overseas.
ANS was pegged $19.80-20.00 a barrel, tracking a 95-cent rise on spot WTI, which ended $21.35-45 a barrel Monday, traders said..
Kern River crude was unchanged early Friday at $14.01/14.11 a barrel.
Wilmington and Line 63 markets remained idle.
